reason: A 60-person, $250M-ARR regulated banking platform doubling headcount YoY is asking a single live Senior Infrastructure/Platform Engineer hire to be 'focused on owning and scaling the foundation of our banking platform as we grow fast' — a public confession that the platform/ops layer under first-time CTO Kevin Bai has no dedicated owner, which is precisely the situation Ben Cole's fractional technical-operations practice exists for.

talk_track: Ben Cole here — I build the platform, DevSecOps, and FinOps layer underneath CTOs; at Lexipol that meant a first-attempt SOC 2 Type II in a CJIS-regulated environment and 22% off the AWS bill, after scaling the same layer at Expedia and Pokemon. Slash's live Senior Infrastructure/Platform Engineer posting asks one hire to be 'focused on owning and scaling the foundation of our banking platform as we grow fast.' Read plainly, that says the foundation of a $250M-ARR banking platform has no dedicated owner yet. At 100% year-over-year headcount growth, that is usually the moment cloud spend starts drifting and enterprise buyers start asking for compliance evidence a single engineer cannot produce alone. Worth having even if we never speak: the fix is an accountable ops layer under the CTO, not more headcount. What do enterprise customers ask Slash for before they sign?
